decisions.reason: The existing same-message Hero V event captures the structural geometry changes but omits the explicit requirement to resolve that geometry in black and white before applying color or metallic treatment.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Thank you for pulling back and studying the V on its own. I believe that is precisely the direction we should take. Before returning to the complete wordmark, I want to keep investigating the V because I think that is where the brand’s identity will be defined.

At this stage, everything should remain entirely black and white. Champagne metallic is still included in the long-term vision, but I don’t want color affecting our choices yet. Geometry needs to be resolved first. The material treatment should strengthen the design rather than determine it.

The V’s right arm needs significantly more investigation. Instead of reading as merely another letter stroke, it should become fundamental to the V’s construction. I want to test variations in its proportion, width, length, and termination so that it feels deliberate without turning decorative.

Its beauty must arise from proportion, geometry, and construction rather than from applied details. Each decision should appear structural, not stylistic.

We also need to keep the larger goal in view. If ELLVÉ were removed, the initial V should remain unmistakably identifiable as vellvé. That is the degree of distinction I want us to reach. When that is solved, I believe the rest of the wordmark will develop naturally.

value_updates.right_arm_role: A fundamental structural feature distinguished through proportion, width, length, and termination rather than decoration.
value_updates.geometry_principle: Beauty must arise from proportion, geometry, and construction rather than applied stylistic details.
value_updates.application_constraint: Resolve the V geometry in black and white before applying color or champagne metallic treatment; material treatment should strengthen the design rather than determine it.

decisions.reason: The kerning requirement was already deferred while the V foundation is developed, and delaying metallic treatment does not alter its spacing or rhythm criteria.
The E and L work was already deferred, and the material sequencing decision does not change the retained architectural letterform criteria.
Champagne metallic remains in the long-term vision, so the accent's required derivation from and correspondence with the Hero V remains valid without modification.
The source focuses the new structural investigation on the opening Hero V and does not change the closing V's required construction relationship.
